mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen for two consecutive weeks (0.4 to -2.7). Own-series momentum implies this downward trend persists absent a reversing shock, so the next-4-week mean stays below the last-4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined from 1.3 to -2.7 over the last two weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean exceeds its 28-day trailing mean despite two consecutive weeks of decline, indicating momentum does not persist.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week collapse in TRANSIT (9.1 to -3.0) signals households curtailing trips outside the home, which mechanically reduces discretionary retail and recreation visits over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week drop exceeds 5 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from 9.1 to -3.0 between t-2w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next two weeks following a TRANSIT week-on-week drop greater than 5 points, in a majority of comparable instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous WORKPLACES decline (11.9 to 9.7) and RESIDENTIAL rise (-2.0 to 0.0) jointly indicate a shift toward home-centered routines; their co-movement amplifies the reduction in retail visits beyond what either series predicts alone.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls and RESIDENTIAL rises in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell while RESIDENTIAL rose over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward mean is not lower than its trailing mean when WORKPLACES declines and RESIDENTIAL rises concurrently for two or more weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A panic-buying regime, evidenced by GROCERY_PHARM surging from 1.7 to 11.4 over three weeks, reallocates household spending and trips toward essential grocery/pharmacy outlets and away from discretionary retail and recreation venues for the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 1.7 to 11.4 while RETAIL_REC fell from 0.4 to -2.7 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean does not fall below its trailing mean despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining elevated above 10 points, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility declines by more than 2 points week-on-week, it signals early employer-driven work-from-home policy adoption ahead of formal government mandates, which quickly suppresses commute-linked retail footfall within one week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week decline exceeds 2 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined from 11.6 to 9.7 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week immediately following a WORKPLACES week-on-week decline exceeding 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: Sydney's transition into autumn reduces daylight and outdoor comfort, independently lowering PARKS activity and the incidental retail footfall tied to outdoor leisure trips, dragging RETAIL_REC down over the next month regardless of pandemic-specific drivers.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 5.0 to -12.1 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward mean rises despite a sustained seasonal decline in PARKS, indicating no seasonal linkage between outdoor and retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: Under a tightening-restriction regime, compounding declines in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT interact to amplify the drop in RETAIL_REC beyond the sum of their individual effects, because reduced commuting and reduced transit access jointly eliminate incidental shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both decline in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT declined simultaneously from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean does not fall more than predicted by either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone when both decline concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid stockpiling surge, defined by GROCERY_PHARM rising more than 5 points week-on-week while RETAIL_REC simultaneously declines, indicates consumers front-loading essential purchases in anticipation of restrictions, which depresses discretionary retail activity in the immediate following week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week increase exceeds 5 percentage points while RETAIL_REC declines
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 3.3 to 10.3 while RETAIL_REC fell from 1.3 to -0.6 between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week following a GROCERY_PHARM surge exceeding 5 points, indicating no short-term substitution effect.
